svg.title: IL-PROOF-021 Four coordination strategies, one frozen corpus - comparison
svg.desc: CONTROLLED LOCAL EVALUATION. Frozen evidence: Uncoordinated 2/2/2/2 Global-lock 0/2/0/2 Per-target-lock 2/2/2/2 Interlock 0/2/2/2 Non-claim: bounded to this sixteen-scenario corpus; Interlock is not universally safe and not safer than locking; no interval or significance is claimed

svg.text: IS THE PER-TARGET LOCK A REAL LOCK?

text.font-family: Courier, 'Courier New', Menlo, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', 'Liberation Mono', monospace
Courier, 'Courier New', Menlo, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', 'Liberation Mono', monospace
Courier, 'Courier New', Menlo, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', 'Liberation Mono', monospace
Helvetica, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, 'Liberation Sans', sans-serif

svg.text: It locked exactly what a lock can see. A composition hazard spanning two lock keys is not visible to any per-key discipline.

text.font-family: Helvetica, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, 'Liberation Sans', sans-serif

svg.text: Global locking preserved safety by eliminating concurrency. Per-target locking preserved concurrency but missed every cross-target composition hazard. Interlock is

text.font-family: Helvetica, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, 'Liberation Sans', sans-serif

svg.text: the only arm in both left-hand columns at once on this corpus.
